newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MINISTER'S DAUGHTER LEAKS EXAM PAPER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MINISTER'S DAUGHTER LEAKS EXAM PAPER.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Education Minister Edmund Garwe has admitted his daughter leaked an examination paper at her school, the state-owned Herald newspaper reported on Wednesday.

It quoted Garwe as saying he had taken some examination papers to a meeting to discuss their reprinting after errors were discovered on them. His daughter, a student at a private school in Harare, got hold of the papers after he left them lying at home, he said.
"I have no excuse for this. It should never have happened and I am very sorry about it," Garwe said, adding that he had voluntarily withdrawn his daughter from writing the examination.
Education Secretary Ignatius Chigwedere said the Zimbabwe Schools Examination Council had completed investigations into the issue. It had yet to make its findings public.
Zimbabwean schools have in the past two years been hit by leakages of examination papers and Chigwedere said the council had recommended measures to plug future leaks.
